summary.oneLiner: Record quarterly profitability — EBITDA margin **>21% (22%)**, PAT >INR20 cr, +575-638 bps margin expansion YoY — validating the multi-year mix-shift into value-added MRP/Reclaim/PCMB and better raw-material optionality. Revenue +20% YoY (consol INR156 cr). The next legs — **TPO (pyrolysis oil) commercial from Q2**, **rCB from Q3-Q4**, PCMB to 10% of revenue, and four international nodes (Oman turned around, S.Africa/Saudi ramping, new Chile sourcing) — underwrite the reiterated **Vision-2029: INR1,000 cr / >18% EBITDA / >30% ROCE**. Watch: ex-EPR underlying PBT growth is muted, and guidance is deliberately capped at 18-20% despite the 22% print.

Revenue +20% YoY (consol INR156 cr). The next legs — **TPO (pyrolysis oil) commercial from Q2**, **rCB from Q3-Q4**, PCMB to 10% of revenue, and four international nodes (Oman turned around, S.Africa/Saudi ramping, new Chile sourcing) — underwrite the reiterated **Vision-2029: INR1,000 cr / >18% EBITDA / >30% ROCE**. Watch: ex-EPR underlying PBT growth is muted, and guidance is deliberately capped at 18-20% despite the 22% print.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1FY27 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue (consol) | ~INR 156 cr | +20% | standalone +18% |
| EBITDA | **>INR 30 cr** | — | margin **>21% (22%)**; standalone +638 bps, consol +575 bps YoY |
| PAT | **>INR 20 cr** (~INR21 cr) | — | margin >13%; standalone +471 bps, consol +416 bps YoY |
| Working-capital days | ~50 (blended) | — | stable ±5% over 2-3 yrs |
| Capex (quarter) | INR 27 cr | — | of ~INR100 cr FY27-28 plan (INR60 cr in FY27) |
| Renewable power share | 51% of production | — | RE capacity 1.23→4.48 MW (~3x); INR1.19 cr green-sourcing savings in qtr |
> **Transcript caveat:** the COO section reads "EBITDA exceeding INR50 crores" (p.5) — this is a **transcription error**; consistent with revenue INR156 cr × ~21% margin and the JMD's "EBITDA exceeding INR30 crores," EBITDA is ~INR30-33 cr. **EPR one-off:** ~100,000 EPR credits (~INR2,500/unit ≈ INR25 cr) monetized to cash this quarter but P&L-recognized in prior years (knocked off vs FY25-26 unbilled revenue) — not a Q1 P&L boost.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue FY27: INR675-700 cr** (reiterated); Vision-2029 target **INR1,000 cr by FY29** at **25%+ revenue CAGR, 33%+ profit CAGR, >18% EBITDA margin, >30% ROCE, 10 locations**.
- **Margin:** guided **18-20%** (aspiration 18%+) despite 22% delivered — cautious on front-ended new-business costs; management calls 18-20% "sustainable/systemic."
- **Capacity:** tire-crushing **185,000 → 235,000 tpa (+27%) by FY27**; MRP expansion **+3,500 tpa commissioning Q3FY27 → 20,000 tpa** (claimed world's largest); blended utilization **75-80% by fiscal-end**.
- **New products:** **TPO (Varle)** — trial Q1, **commercial sales Q2**, stabilise Q3; **rCB** — production Q3, **commercial sales Q4**; TPO+rCB together **7-10% of FY27 revenue (~INR50-60 cr)**.
- **Segments:** **TP Buildtech >30% growth, cross INR100 cr revenue FY27**; **PCMB → 10% of FY27 revenue**; **Steel Abrasives ~50% volume growth FY27** (Zibo TAA China distributorship, customer transition Q4FY27).
- **International:** Mbodla (S.Africa) **breakeven Q2FY27**, Phase-2 tire-recycling production Q2/Q3; Saudi 24,000 tpa **construction start end-CY2026** (geopolitics permitting).
- **Capex ~INR100 cr FY27-28** (INR60 cr FY27); **R&D INR5 cr FY27**.
order book & pipeline: Not order-book-driven, but: secured a **15,000-t rubberized-bitumen processing order** for FY27 execution; exclusive India distributorship of **Zibo TAA Metal Technology (China)** for steel abrasives (~50% volume-growth target); robust export pipeline (+46% YoY). Registered as authorized plastics recycler → EPR credit generation from plastics from 1-Apr-2026.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Tire recycling:** utilization 88% India / 78% Oman; India tire-crushing volume **+35% YoY** (seq -10% on softer consumer demand); MRP **+28%**, Reclaim **+37%** YoY.
- **Industrial:** volume +27%, **revenue +58% YoY** (MRP + customer adds + exports); demand from tire-maker ESG/EPR pressure and rising RM costs.
- **Infrastructure:** revenue +7% (volume +33%) — West-Asia bitumen shortage/price spike made **rubberized bitumen the cost-effective alternative** (a demand tailwind); Emulsion impacted by supply constraints.
- **Consumer (turfing):** volume **-20%** — binder/synthetic-grass prices ~tripled (import disruption) delaying track/turf projects; ~8-10% of business, expected to bounce back on stabilisation.
- **Steel:** stable (marginal volume dip, better realization); Zibo distributorship added.
- **PCMB:** revenue **tripled to INR12 cr** (vs INR4 cr); 8% of topline → target 10% FY27; capacity **6,000 → 18,000 tpa** (Haryana), toward ~60% utilization.
- **Global Recycle Oman:** revenue ~INR9 cr, EBITDA margin **8.53%**, PAT INR0.34 cr (+31% over FY26) — recovered via RM import into Oman.
- **Mbodla (S.Africa) + Saudi:** combined loss ~INR53 lakh (startup); S.Africa Phase-1 done, semi-processed exports begun.
- **TP Buildtech:** revenue INR19 cr, EBITDA INR3 cr; acquiring land in Western Maharashtra for new construction-chemicals facility.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **TPO + rCB (pyrolysis)** — the new high-value leg, commercial from Q2/Q3, ~INR50-60 cr in FY27.
- **PCMB** scaling to 18,000 tpa; **Steel Abrasives** via Zibo; **TP Buildtech** to >INR100 cr.
- **International sourcing/hedge:** Chile (new) + South Africa secure end-of-life-tire feedstock; Oman/Saudi are Middle-East processing bases. Possible **new greenfield India plant / de-bottlenecking** as domestic demand is "very robust" at 80-85% utilization.
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Value-added scale + technology in MRP:** from <100 t/month (2015-16) to 20,000 tpa capacity; "technology efficiency… long customer-onboarding process… more resilient and committed than competition" — high switching cost/qualification barrier.
- **Multi-segment hedge:** consumer/industrial/infra/steel/PCMB/TPO/rCB diversification cushions any single geopolitical or cyclical shock (explicitly framed as the durability edge).
- **Feedstock optionality:** diversified ELP sourcing (India + Chile + S.Africa + Oman imports) controls RM cost — the stated driver of this quarter's gross-margin expansion.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross-margin expansion (the bulk of the ~4% EBITDA-margin jump) from (i) more efficient/optional raw-material sourcing and (ii) higher value-added product mix — management calls these **systemic, not one-off** (marginal inventory gain only). Material+inventory-to-sales fell to ~46% (from >51%). Offset: front-ended costs of new geographies (Saudi/S.Africa) and new plants → why 18-20% is guided vs 22% delivered.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): ~INR100 cr over FY27-28 (INR27 cr spent in Q1; INR60 cr to be capitalised FY27). Commissioning watch-list: MRP +3,500 tpa (Q3), TPO commercial (Q2)/stabilise (Q3), rCB (Q3 production → Q4 sales), tire-crushing to 235k tpa (FY27), Saudi construction (end-CY26), S.Africa Phase-2 (Q2/Q3). Management signals capex could rise if demand stays strong.
capital allocation: Core investment stays **India** ("for the foreseeable future"); international nodes are hedges/sourcing, not the primary capital sink. INR5 cr to R&D (recycled-rubber + engineered plastics + recovered-fiber TPO). RE build-out (rooftop solar Gummidipoondi 999 kW / Varle 2,218 kW; RE 51% of power) to cut energy cost. WC disciplined at ~50 days.
risks & watch-items:
- **EPR dependency:** ~INR25-30 cr/yr at PBT level (stable) — ex-EPR, underlying PBT growth is muted (analyst math: FY26 PBT INR72 cr − INR21 cr EPR ≈ INR51 cr; Q1 PBT INR28 cr − ~INR5 cr EPR ≈ INR23 cr). EPR accounting (recognised on portal reflection, monetised later) distorts QoQ comparability.
- **West-Asia geopolitics:** double-edged — helps infra (rubberized-bitumen substitution) but hurts consumer/turfing (imported binder prices tripled) and Oman/Saudi logistics; management concedes a severe global escalation would hit everyone.
- **New-geography startup losses** (S.Africa/Saudi) and **new-product ramp** (TPO/rCB) are front-ended costs before revenue.
- **Q2 seasonality** (monsoon) on infrastructure; delayed monsoon a mild positive this year.
- Guidance-vs-delivery gap (18-20% guide vs 22% print) — manage expectations.
management quality / tone: Confident but deliberately conservative (JMD Gaurav Sekhri repeatedly reframes 22% down to an 18-20% "guidance," citing front-ended costs). Transparent — if repetitive — on the EPR accounting nuance under persistent analyst probing; candid that ex-EPR growth is optical-heavy. COO Subodh detailed on segments; CFO Abhay crisp on capex phasing (INR60 cr FY27). Credible execution track record on MRP scale-up.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **The clean read is EPR-adjusted:** EPR (~INR25-30 cr/yr PBT, stable) is now "integral" but flat — so the growth engine is genuinely the volume/mix shift (MRP +28%, Reclaim +37%, exports +46%, Industrial rev +58%), not EPR.
- **This quarter's EPR cash (~INR25 cr) is a balance-sheet event** (inventory→cash), not a P&L event — analysts repeatedly conflated the two; management held the line.
- **Vision re-labelled 2028 → 2029** (INR1,000 cr now by FY29) and near-term crushing target sharpened to **235k tpa by FY27** (vs "250k by FY28" last covered quarter) — a modest timeline/scope reset.
- **New Chile subsidiary** signals feedstock security is becoming a strategic priority (hedging global ELP supply), alongside S.Africa.
- Rubberized bitumen is structurally advantaged by permanent Indian bitumen-import dependence + government import-reduction push — a durable infra tailwind independent of the current price spike.

themes.title: Specialty packaging & sustainable materials
themes.need: Premiumization, e-commerce and a sustainability/recycling mandate drive a packaging up-cycle across flexible films, rigid plastics, cartons and compostables. UFLEX/EPL/HUHTAMAKI/COSMOFIRST/ESTER on films/tubes; TCPLPACK/AGI/BOROLTD on cartons/glass; MOLDTKPAC/MOLDTECH on rigid/IML; PAKKA/GANECOS on compostable & recycled materials.
themes.driver: Brand-owner restocking; export demand recovery; recycled-content mandates; commodity-cost pass-through.
